also_known_as.en: The Old Man of the Morea

summary.en: Klepht, mercenary officer in British service on Zakynthos, and the most capable Greek commander of the War of Independence. He took Tripolitsa in 1821 and broke Dramali's army at Dervenakia in 1822.

body_html.en:
Kolokotronis came from a family of klephts and armatoloi in Messenia and spent the years before 1821 in Ionian exile, where he served as an officer in a Greek regiment raised by the British. He landed in the Mani in March 1821 and within six months had reduced Tripolitsa, the Ottoman administrative centre of the Peloponnese.

His victory at Dervenakia in July 1822 destroyed the army sent to reconquer the Morea and made him the dominant military figure of the revolution. It also made him a faction leader. He was imprisoned by the civil government on Hydra in 1825, released to face Ibrahim Pasha, and later sentenced to death under the Bavarian regency before Otto pardoned him. His memoirs, dictated in 1836, remain the classic account of the war from the inside.
